title.zh: 卷一百六十九 列傳第五十七 高穀 胡濙 王直
title.en: Volume 169 Biographies 57: Gao Gu, Hu Ying, Wang Zhi
title.raw: 卷一百六十九 列傳第五十七 高穀 胡濙 王直 Volume 169 Biographies 57: Gao Gu, Hu Ying, Wang Zhi

sentences.zh: 高谷胡濙王直

translations.literal: Gao Gu, Hu Ying, Wang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu, Hu Ying, and Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，進尚書，兼翰林學士，掌閣務如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign, he was promoted to Minister, concurrently Hanlin Academician, managing Grand Secretariat affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingtai reign, he was promoted to minister and appointed concurrent Hanlin Academician, continuing to manage Grand Secretariat affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 英宗將還，奉迎禮薄，千戶龔遂榮投書於谷，具言禮宜從厚，援唐肅宗迎上皇故事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was about to return, the welcoming ceremony was meager. Battalion officer Gong Suirong sent a letter to Gao Gu, fully stating that the rites ought to be generous, citing the precedent of Tang Suzong welcoming the retired emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was about to return, the planned welcome ceremony was judged too thin. Battalion officer Gong Suirong sent Gao Gu a letter arguing at length that the rites should be generous, citing the Tang precedent of Emperor Suzong welcoming the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 谷袖之入朝，遍示廷臣曰：「武夫尚知禮，況儒臣乎！

translations.literal: Gao Gu tucked it in his sleeve and entered court, showing it to all court officials and saying: "Even a military man knows propriety—how much more should a Confucian minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu tucked the letter in his sleeve and brought it to court, showing it to officials throughout the assembly. "Even a soldier understands propriety," he said, "how much more should a Confucian minister!"

sentences.zh: 」眾善其言。

translations.literal: The assembly approved of his words.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly approved of what he said.

sentences.zh: 胡濙、王直欲以聞。

translations.literal: Hu Ying and Wang Zhi wished to report it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying and Wang Zhi wanted to bring the matter to the emperor's attention.

sentences.zh: 谷曰：「迎復議上，上意久不決。

translations.literal: Gao Gu said: "The plan to welcome him back has been submitted repeatedly, and His Majesty's mind has long been unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu said, "The proposal to welcome him back has been submitted again and again, yet His Majesty's mind has long remained unsettled."

sentences.zh: 若進此書，使上知朝野同心，亦一助也。

translations.literal: If we submit this letter, letting His Majesty know that court and countryside are of one mind, that would also be some help.
translations.idiomatic: If we submit this letter and let His Majesty see that court and countryside are of one mind, that would help move the matter forward.

sentences.zh: 」都御史王文不可。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen objected.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen would not agree.

sentences.zh: 已而言官奏之。

translations.literal: Soon after, censorial officials memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, censorial officials memorialized about the matter.

sentences.zh: 詰所從得，谷對曰：「自臣所。

translations.literal: When questioned where it came from, Gao Gu replied: "From my office."
translations.idiomatic: When asked where the letter had come from, Gao Gu answered, "From my office."

sentences.zh: 」因抗章懇請如遂榮言。

translations.literal: He then submitted a forthright memorial earnestly requesting what Suirong had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a forthright memorial earnestly urging that Suirong's proposal be adopted.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不從，亦不之罪。

translations.literal: Though the emperor did not agree, he did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept the proposal, but he did not punish Gao Gu.

sentences.zh: 二年進少保、東閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign he was promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 易儲，加太子太傅，給二俸。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was changed, he was additionally made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and granted two salaries.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was replaced, he was additionally appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and granted two salaries.

sentences.zh: 應天、鳳陽災，命祀三陵，振貧民。

translations.literal: When disasters struck Yingtian and Fengyang, he was ordered to offer sacrifices at the three imperial tombs and relieve the impoverished populace.
translations.idiomatic: When disasters struck Yingtian and Fengyang, he was ordered to sacrifice at the three imperial tombs and provide relief to the poor.

sentences.zh: 七年進謹身殿大學士，仍兼東閣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Self-Discipline, still concurrently serving in the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Self-Discipline while retaining his concurrent post in the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 內閣七人，言論多齟齬。

translations.literal: The seven members of the Grand Secretariat often clashed in their opinions.
translations.idiomatic: Among the seven members of the Grand Secretariat, opinions frequently clashed.

sentences.zh: 谷清直，持議正。

translations.literal: Gao Gu was upright and incorruptible, holding to correct positions in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu was upright and incorruptible, and he held firm to correct positions in debate.

sentences.zh: 王文由谷薦，數擠谷。

translations.literal: Wang Wen had been recommended by Gao Gu, yet repeatedly pushed him aside.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen had been recommended by Gao Gu, yet repeatedly worked to push him aside.

sentences.zh: 谷屢請解機務，不許。

translations.literal: Gao Gu repeatedly requested to be relieved of secretarial duties, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu repeatedly asked to be relieved of secretarial duties, but his requests were denied.

sentences.zh: 都給事中林聰忤權要論死，谷力救，得薄譴。

translations.literal: When chief supervising secretary Lin Cong offended powerful figures and was sentenced to death, Gao Gu vigorously intervened to save him, and Lin received only a mild reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: When chief supervising secretary Lin Cong offended powerful figures and was sentenced to death, Gao Gu intervened forcefully on his behalf, and Lin received only a mild reprimand.

sentences.zh: 陳循及文構考官劉儼、黃諫，帝命禮部會谷復閱試卷。

translations.literal: Chen Xun and Wang Wen framed examination officials Liu Yan and Huang Jian; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to join with Gao Gu in re-examining the examination papers.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun and Wang Wen framed the examination officials Liu Yan and Huang Jian, and the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to join Gao Gu in re-examining the papers.

sentences.zh: 谷力言儼等無私，且曰：「貴胄與寒士競進，已不可。

translations.literal: Gao Gu forcefully argued that Liu Yan and others had shown no favoritism, and said: "For noble scions and poor scholars to compete for advancement is already unacceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu argued forcefully that Liu Yan and the others had shown no favoritism, saying, "For noble scions and poor scholars to compete for advancement is already unacceptable."

sentences.zh: 況不安義命，欲因此構考官乎？

translations.literal: How much worse when they, discontent with their allotted fate, wish to use this to frame the examiners?
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when men discontent with their allotted fate seek to use this to frame the examiners?

sentences.zh: 」帝乃賜循、文子中式，惟黜林挺一人，事得已。

translations.literal: The emperor then granted Chen Xun's and Wang Wen's sons passage in the examinations, dismissed only Lin Ting, and the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then allowed Chen Xun's and Wang Wen's sons to pass the examinations, dismissed only Lin Ting, and the affair was closed.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，循、文等皆誅竄，谷謝病。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Chen Xun, Wang Wen, and others were all executed or banished, and Gao Gu claimed illness to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Chen Xun, Wang Wen, and the others were executed or banished, and Gao Gu retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 英宗謂谷長者，語廷臣曰：「谷在內閣議迎駕及南內事，嘗左右朕。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong called Gao Gu a man of worthy character and told court officials: "When Gao Gu was in the Grand Secretariat debating the welcome of the imperial carriage and matters of the Southern Palace, he often guided me."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong called Gao Gu a man of worthy character and told the court, "When Gao Gu served in the Grand Secretariat and debated the welcome of the imperial carriage and matters of the Southern Palace, he often guided me."

sentences.zh: 其賜金帛襲衣，給驛舟以歸。

translations.literal: He was granted gold, silks, and ceremonial robes, and given an imperial courier boat for his return home.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu was granted gold, silks, and ceremonial robes, and an imperial courier boat was provided for his journey home.

sentences.zh: 」尋復賜敕獎諭。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again granted an edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he received another edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 谷既去位，杜門絕賓客。

translations.literal: After Gao Gu left office, he shut his doors and refused visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao Gu had left office, he shut his doors and refused all visitors.

sentences.zh: 有問景泰、天順間事，輒不應。

translations.literal: When asked about events during the Jingtai and Tianshun reigns, he would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone asked about events during the Jingtai and Tianshun reigns, he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 天順四年正月卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died in the first month of the fourth year of Tianshun, at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the fourth year of Tianshun, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 谷美豐儀，樂儉素，位至臺司，敝廬瘠田而已。

translations.literal: Gao Gu had a handsome bearing and delighted in frugality; though he reached the highest ministerial rank, he owned only a humble dwelling and lean fields.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu had a handsome bearing and loved plain living; though he rose to the highest ministerial rank, he owned only a humble dwelling and lean fields.

sentences.zh: 成化初，贈太保，謚文義。

translations.literal: In the early Chenghua reign, he was posthumously given the title of Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chenghua reign he was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian and given the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 胡濙，字源潔，武進人。

translations.literal: Hu Ying, courtesy name Yuanjie, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying, courtesy name Yuanjie, was a native of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 生而發白，彌月乃黑。

translations.literal: He was born with white hair, which turned black only after a full month.
translations.idiomatic: He was born with white hair, which did not turn black until he was a month old.

sentences.zh: 建文二年舉進士，授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jianwen reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jianwen reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年遷戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Yongle reign he was transferred to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongle reign he was transferred to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 惠帝之崩於火，或言遁去，諸舊臣多從者，帝疑之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huidi died in the palace fire, some said he had escaped, and many former ministers were said to have followed him; the emperor was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huidi died in the palace fire, some said he had escaped, and many former ministers were rumored to have gone with him, which aroused the emperor's suspicion.

sentences.zh: 五年遣濙頒禦制諸書，並訪仙人張邋遢，遍行天下州郡鄉邑，隱察建文帝安在。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor dispatched Hu Ying to distribute imperial works and to seek out the immortal Zhang Tuo, touring every prefecture, district, and township in the realm while secretly investigating where Emperor Jianwen might be.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor sent Hu Ying to distribute imperial works and to seek out the immortal Zhang Tuo, traveling through every prefecture, district, and township in the realm while secretly searching for Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 濙以故在外最久，至十四年乃還。

translations.literal: For this reason Hu Ying remained abroad longest, not returning until the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Hu Ying remained abroad longer than anyone else and did not return until the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 所至，亦間以民隱聞。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, he also occasionally reported on the people's hidden grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went, he also occasionally reported the people's hidden grievances.

sentences.zh: 母喪乞歸，不許，擢禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: When his mother died he requested leave to mourn but was not permitted; instead he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he asked to return home for mourning, but permission was denied and he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites instead.

sentences.zh: 十七年復出巡江浙、湖、湘諸府。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was again sent out on inspection to the Jiang-Zhe and Hu-Xiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was again dispatched on inspection tours through the Jiang-Zhe and Hu-Xiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二十一年還朝，馳謁帝於宣府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he returned to court and hurried to audience with the emperor at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he returned to court and hurried to audience with the emperor at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 帝已就寢，聞濙至，急起召入。

translations.literal: The emperor had already retired for the night, but hearing of Hu Ying's arrival, he rose urgently to summon him in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already retired for the night, but when he heard that Hu Ying had arrived, he rose at once and summoned him in.

sentences.zh: 濙悉以所聞對，漏下四鼓乃出。

translations.literal: Hu Ying answered fully with everything he had learned, and did not leave until the fourth watch.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying reported everything he had learned, and did not leave until the fourth watch.

sentences.zh: 先濙未至，傳言建文帝蹈海去，帝分遣內臣鄭和數輩浮海下西洋，至是疑始釋。

translations.literal: Before Hu Ying's return, rumor had circulated that Emperor Jianwen had fled overseas, so the emperor had dispatched eunuchs including Zheng He on several voyages across the seas to the Western Ocean; only now was his suspicion finally eased.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hu Ying returned, rumor had held that Emperor Jianwen had fled overseas, and the emperor had dispatched eunuchs including Zheng He on several voyages across the seas to the Western Ocean; only now was his suspicion finally put to rest.

sentences.zh: 皇太子監國南京，漢王為飛語謗太子。

translations.literal: While the crown prince governed at Nanjing as regent, the Prince of Han spread slanderous rumors against the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: While the crown prince governed at Nanjing as regent, the Prince of Han spread slanderous rumors against him.

sentences.zh: 帝改濙官南京，因命廉之。

translations.literal: The emperor transferred Hu Ying's office to Nanjing and ordered him to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor transferred Hu Ying's post to Nanjing and ordered him to investigate.

sentences.zh: 濙至，密疏馳上監國七事，言誠敬孝謹無他，帝悅。

translations.literal: When Hu Ying arrived, he sent a secret memorial reporting seven points on the regency, stating that the crown prince was sincere, reverent, filial, and cautious with no other fault; the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Ying arrived, he sent a secret memorial reporting seven points on the regency, attesting that the crown prince was sincere, reverent, filial, and cautious and had no other fault, and the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，仍遷禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Xuande Emperor ascended the throne, Hu Ying was again transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuande Emperor ascended the throne, Hu Ying was again appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明年來朝，乃留行在禮部，尋進尚書。

translations.literal: The following year he came to audience at court and was retained to serve at the mobile capital's Ministry of Rites, soon advancing to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came to court for audience and was retained at the mobile capital's Ministry of Rites, soon advancing to minister.

sentences.zh: 漢王反，與楊榮等贊親征。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Han rebelled, he joined Yang Rong and others in urging a personal campaign by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Han rebelled, he joined Yang Rong and others in urging the emperor to lead the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 事平，賚予甚厚。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, rewards were lavish.

sentences.zh: 明年賜第長安右門外，給閽者二人，賜銀章四。

translations.literal: The following year he was granted a residence outside Chang'an Gate on the right, given two gatekeepers, and bestowed four silver seals.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was granted a residence outside Chang'an Gate on the right, given two gatekeepers, and bestowed four silver seals.

sentences.zh: 生辰，賜宴其第。

translations.literal: On his birthday, the emperor granted a banquet at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: On his birthday the emperor granted a banquet at his residence.

sentences.zh: 四年命兼理詹事府事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to concurrently manage the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was ordered to concurrently manage affairs of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 六年，張本卒，又兼領行在戶部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Zhang Ben died, he additionally took charge of the mobile capital's Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, after Zhang Ben died, he additionally took charge of the mobile capital's Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時國用漸廣，濙慮度支不足，蠲租詔下，輒沮格。

translations.literal: At that time state expenditures gradually expanded; Hu Ying worried about insufficient revenue and habitually blocked edicts remitting taxes.
translations.idiomatic: As state expenditures gradually expanded, Hu Ying worried that revenue would not suffice and habitually blocked edicts remitting taxes.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗切戒之，然眷遇不少替。

translations.literal: The emperor often warned him sternly, yet favor toward him never diminished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often warned him sternly, yet his favor toward Hu Ying never diminished.

sentences.zh: 嘗曲宴濙及楊士奇、夏原吉、蹇義，曰：「海內無虞，卿等四人力也。

translations.literal: The emperor once held a private banquet for Hu Ying, Yang Shiqi, Xia Yuanji, and Jian Yi, saying: "Within the seas there is no trouble—the four of you are the reason."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once held a private banquet for Hu Ying, Yang Shiqi, Xia Yuanji, and Jian Yi, saying, "The realm is at peace, and the four of you deserve the credit."

sentences.zh: 」英宗即位，詔節冗費。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, an edict ordered the reduction of wasteful expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, an edict ordered the reduction of wasteful expenditures.

sentences.zh: 濙因奏減上供物，及汰法王以下番僧四五百人，浮費大省。

translations.literal: Hu Ying memorialized to reduce tribute goods and to dismiss four or five hundred Tibetan monks below the Dharma King rank, yielding large savings in wasteful spending.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying memorialized to reduce tribute goods and to dismiss four or five hundred Tibetan monks below the rank of Dharma King, producing large savings in wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 正統五年，山西災，詔行寬恤，既而有采買物料之命。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong, when Shanxi suffered disaster, an edict was issued for lenient relief, yet soon afterward came an order to procure materials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengtong, when Shanxi suffered disaster, an edict was issued for lenient relief, yet soon afterward came an order to procure materials.

sentences.zh: 濙上疏言詔旨宜信。

translations.literal: Hu Ying memorialized that imperial edicts ought to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying memorialized that imperial edicts ought to be honored in practice.

sentences.zh: 又言軍旗營求差遣，因而擾民，宜罷之。

translations.literal: He also said that military households seeking official assignments were thereby harassing the people and that this practice should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that military households seeking official assignments were harassing the people and that the practice should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 行在禮部印失，詔弗問，命改鑄。

translations.literal: The seal of the mobile capital's Ministry of Rites was lost; the emperor ordered no inquiry and commanded that a new one be cast.
translations.idiomatic: The seal of the mobile capital's Ministry of Rites was lost; the emperor ordered no inquiry and commanded that a new one be cast.

sentences.zh: 已，又失，被劾下獄。

translations.literal: Soon it was lost again, and he was impeached and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it was lost again, and he was impeached and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，印獲，復職。

translations.literal: Before long the seal was recovered and he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the seal was recovered and he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 九年，年七十，乞致仕，不許。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at age seventy, he requested retirement but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, at the age of seventy, he requested retirement but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，群臣聚哭於朝，有議南遷者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was captured on the northern campaign, officials gathered weeping at court, and some proposed moving the capital south.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was captured on the northern campaign, officials gathered weeping at court, and some proposed moving the capital south.

sentences.zh: 濙曰：「文皇定陵寢於此，示子孫以不拔之計也。

translations.literal: Hu Ying said: "Emperor Taizong established the imperial tombs here, showing posterity a resolve never to withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying said, "Emperor Taizong established the imperial tombs here to show posterity a resolve never to withdraw."

sentences.zh: 」與侍郎于謙合，中外始有固誌。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Minister Yu Qian, he stiffened resolve throughout court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Vice Minister Yu Qian, he stiffened resolve throughout court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，進太子太傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingtai ascended the throne, Hu Ying was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingtai ascended the throne, Hu Ying was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 楊善使也先，濙言上皇蒙塵久，宜附進服食，不報。

translations.literal: When Yang Shan was sent as envoy to Esen, Hu Ying proposed that as the retired emperor had long suffered captivity, food and clothing ought to be sent along, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shan was sent as envoy to Esen, Hu Ying proposed that as the retired emperor had long suffered captivity, food and clothing ought to be sent along, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 上皇將還，命禮部具奉迎儀。

translations.literal: When the retired emperor was about to return, the Ministry of Rites was ordered to prepare welcoming ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor was about to return, the Ministry of Rites was ordered to prepare the welcoming ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 濙等議遣禮部署迎於龍虎臺，錦衣具法駕迎居庸關，百司迎土城外，諸將迎教場門；

translations.literal: Hu Ying and others proposed that the Ministry of Rites should dispatch officials to welcome him at Longhu Terrace, the Brocade Guard should prepare the imperial carriage to welcome him at Juyong Pass, all offices should welcome him outside Tucheng, and generals should welcome him at the drill ground gate;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying and others proposed that the Ministry of Rites should dispatch officials to welcome him at Longhu Terrace, the Brocade Guard should prepare the imperial carriage to receive him at Juyong Pass, all offices should welcome him outside Tucheng, and generals should welcome him at the drill ground gate;

sentences.zh: 上皇自安定門入，進東安門，於東上北門南面坐；

translations.literal: the retired emperor would enter through Anding Gate, proceed through Dong'an Gate, and take his seat facing south at the northern gate on the east side of the upper palace;
translations.idiomatic: the retired emperor would enter through Anding Gate, proceed through Dong'an Gate, and take his seat facing south at the northern gate on the east side of the upper palace;

sentences.zh: 皇帝謁見畢，百官朝見，上皇入南城大內。

translations.literal: after the emperor performed the audience, all officials would pay court, and the retired emperor would enter the Southern Palace within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: after the emperor performed the audience, all officials would pay court, and the retired emperor would enter the Southern Palace within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 議上，傳旨以一轎二馬迎於居庸關，至安定門易法駕，余如奏。

translations.literal: When the plan was submitted, an imperial message ordered one palanquin and two horses to welcome him at Juyong Pass, switching to the imperial carriage at Anding Gate, with everything else as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was submitted, an imperial message ordered one palanquin and two horses to welcome him at Juyong Pass, with the imperial carriage to be used from Anding Gate onward, and everything else as proposed.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉福等言禮太薄。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Liu Fu and others said the ceremonies were too meager.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Liu Fu and others said the ceremonies were too meager.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：朕尊大兄為太上皇帝，尊禮無加矣。

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "I honor my elder brother as the retired emperor—the honor could not be greater."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I honor my elder brother as the retired emperor; the honor could not be greater."

sentences.zh: 福等顧雲太薄，其意何居？

translations.literal: Why do Fu and the others say the ceremonies are too thin—what is their intent?
translations.idiomatic: Why do Fu and the others say the ceremonies are too thin—what do they mean by that?

sentences.zh: 禮部其會官詳察之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites shall convene officials and investigate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Ministry of Rites convene officials and investigate in detail.

sentences.zh: 」濙等言：「諸臣意無他，欲陛下篤親親耳。

translations.literal: Hu Ying and others said: "The officials mean no harm—they only wish Your Majesty to deepen kinship affection."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying and others said, "The officials mean no harm; they only wish Your Majesty to deepen kinship affection."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「昨得太上皇書，具言迎駕之禮宜從簡損，朕豈得違之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yesterday I received a letter from the retired emperor fully stating that welcoming ceremonies ought to be simplified. How could I disobey?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yesterday I received a letter from the retired emperor stating at length that the welcome ceremony ought to be simplified. How could I disobey?"

sentences.zh: 」群臣乃不敢言。

translations.literal: The officials then did not dare speak further.
translations.idiomatic: The officials then did not dare speak further.

sentences.zh: 會千戶龔遂榮為書投大學士高谷，言奉迎宜厚，具言唐肅宗迎上皇故事。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Battalion Officer Gong Suirong sent a letter to Grand Secretary Gao Gu stating that welcoming ceremonies ought to be generous, citing in full the precedent of Tang Suzong welcoming the retired emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Battalion Officer Gong Suirong sent Grand Secretary Gao Gu a letter arguing that the welcome ceremony ought to be generous, citing at length the Tang precedent of Emperor Suzong welcoming the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 谷袖之以朝，與王直等共觀之。

translations.literal: Gao Gu tucked it in his sleeve and brought it to court, where he and Wang Zhi and others viewed it together.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu tucked the letter in his sleeve and brought it to court, where he and Wang Zhi and others read it together.

sentences.zh: 直與濙欲聞之帝，為都御史王文所阻，而給事中葉盛竟以聞。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi and Hu Ying wanted to report it to the emperor but were blocked by Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen, while supervising secretary Ye Sheng ultimately did report it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi and Hu Ying wanted to report it to the emperor but were blocked by Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen, while supervising secretary Ye Sheng ultimately brought it to the emperor's attention.

sentences.zh: 盛同官林聰復劾直、濙、谷等，皆股肱大臣，有聞必告，不宜偶語竊議。

translations.literal: Ye Sheng's colleague Lin Cong further impeached Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, Gao Gu, and others, saying that as chief ministers they should report anything they heard and ought not whisper and discuss in private.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Sheng's colleague Lin Cong further impeached Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, Gao Gu, and the others, saying that as chief ministers they should report anything they learned and ought not whisper and discuss in private.

sentences.zh: 有詔索書。

translations.literal: An edict was issued demanding the letter.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued demanding the letter.

sentences.zh: 濙等因以書進，且言：「肅宗迎上皇典禮，今日正可仿行。

translations.literal: Hu Ying and the others submitted the letter and said: "The ceremony of Tang Suzong welcoming the retired emperor is precisely what may be followed today."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying and the others submitted the letter and said, "The ceremony by which Tang Suzong welcomed the retired emperor is precisely what may be followed today."

sentences.zh: 陛下宜躬迎安定門外，分遣大臣迎龍虎臺。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought personally to welcome him outside Anding Gate and dispatch ministers separately to welcome him at Longhu Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought to welcome him in person outside Anding Gate and dispatch ministers separately to welcome him at Longhu Terrace.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅曰：「第從朕命，無事紛更。

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased, said: "Just follow my command—do not make needless changes."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, displeased, said, "Just follow my command—do not make needless changes."

sentences.zh: 」上皇至，居南城宮。

translations.literal: When the retired emperor arrived, he resided at the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor arrived, he took up residence in the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 濙請帝明年正旦率群臣朝延安門，不許。

translations.literal: Hu Ying requested that on New Year's Day of the following year the emperor lead officials in audience at Yan'an Gate, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying asked that on New Year's Day of the following year the emperor lead the officials in audience at Yan'an Gate, but this was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 上皇萬壽節，請令百官拜賀延安門，亦不許。

translations.literal: On the retired emperor's birthday, Hu Ying requested that all officials be ordered to offer congratulations at Yan'an Gate, but this too was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the retired emperor's birthday, Hu Ying asked that all officials be ordered to offer congratulations at Yan'an Gate, but this too was denied.

sentences.zh: 三年正月與王直並進少傅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he was jointly promoted with Wang Zhi to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he and Wang Zhi were jointly promoted to Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 易太子，加兼太子太師。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was changed, he was additionally made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was replaced, he was additionally appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 王文惡林聰，文致其罪，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Wang Wen hated Lin Cong, fabricated charges against him, and wished to have him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen hated Lin Cong, fabricated charges against him, and sought to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 濙不肯署，遂稱疾，數日不朝。

translations.literal: Hu Ying refused to sign the document, then claimed illness and did not attend court for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying refused to sign the document, then claimed illness and stayed away from court for several days.

sentences.zh: 帝使興安問疾。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the eunuch Xing'an to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Xing'an to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「老臣本無疾，聞欲殺林聰，殊驚悸耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "This old minister is not actually ill; hearing that Lin Cong was to be killed, I was greatly shaken."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "This old minister is not actually ill; I was simply shaken to hear that Lin Cong was to be killed."

sentences.zh: 」聰由是得釋。

translations.literal: Lin Cong was thereby released.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Cong was thereby released.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，力疾入朝，遂求去。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Hu Ying forced himself to attend court despite illness and then requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Hu Ying forced himself to attend court despite illness and then asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 賜璽書、白金、楮幣、襲衣，給驛，官其一子錦衣，世鎮撫。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial letter, white silver, paper currency, and ceremonial robes, given an imperial courier, and one of his sons was appointed to the Brocade Guard as hereditary garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an imperial letter, white silver, paper currency, and ceremonial robes, given an imperial courier, and one of his sons was appointed to the Brocade Guard as hereditary garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 濙歷事六朝，垂六十年，中外稱耆德。

translations.literal: Hu Ying served through six reigns, spanning nearly sixty years, and was called a venerable worthy throughout court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying served through six reigns, spanning nearly sixty years, and was hailed as a venerable elder throughout court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 及歸，有三弟，年皆七十余，須眉皓白，燕聚一堂，因名之曰「壽愷」。

translations.literal: When he returned home, he had three younger brothers, all over seventy, with white beards and eyebrows; they gathered in one hall for feasting and named it the Hall of Longevity and Joy.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home, he had three younger brothers, all over seventy, with white beards and eyebrows; they gathered in one hall for feasting and named it the Hall of Longevity and Joy.

sentences.zh: 又七年始卒，年八十九。

translations.literal: Seven years later he died, at the age of eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later he died, at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚忠安。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Zhong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian and given the posthumous name Zhong'an.

sentences.zh: 濙節儉寬厚，喜怒不形於色，能以身下人。

translations.literal: Hu Ying was frugal and generous, never showing joy or anger on his face, and could humble himself before others.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying was frugal and generous, never showing joy or anger on his face, and could humble himself before others.

sentences.zh: 在禮部久，表賀祥瑞，以官當首署名，人因謂其性善承迎。

translations.literal: Having long served in the Ministry of Rites, when memorials congratulating auspicious omens were submitted, his office was expected to sign first, and people therefore said he was inclined to flatter.
translations.idiomatic: Having long served in the Ministry of Rites, when memorials congratulating auspicious omens were submitted, his office was expected to sign first, and people therefore said he was inclined to flatter.

sentences.zh: 南城人龔謙多妖術，濙薦為天文生，又薦道士仰彌高曉陰陽兵法，使守邊，時頗譏之。

translations.literal: Gong Qian of the Southern City practiced many occult arts; Hu Ying recommended him as an astronomy student, and also recommended the Daoist Yang Migao, who knew yin-yang and military strategy, to guard the frontier—at the time this was much ridiculed.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Qian of the Southern City practiced many occult arts; Hu Ying recommended him as an astronomy student, and also recommended the Daoist Yang Migao, versed in yin-yang and military strategy, to guard the frontier—at the time this was much ridiculed.

sentences.zh: 王直，字行儉，泰和人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, courtesy name Xingjian, was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, courtesy name Xingjian, was a native of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 父伯貞，洪武十五年以明經聘至京。

translations.literal: His father Wang Bozhen was summoned to the capital in the fifteenth year of Hongwu for his mastery of the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Bozhen was summoned to the capital in the fifteenth year of Hongwu for his mastery of the Classics.

sentences.zh: 時應詔者五百余人，伯貞對第一。

translations.literal: More than five hundred men responded to the imperial summons, and Bozhen ranked first in the examination.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred men responded to the imperial summons, and Bozhen ranked first in the examination.

sentences.zh: 授試僉事，分巡廣東雷州。

translations.literal: He was appointed probationary assistant commissioner and assigned to circuit inspection of Leizhou in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed probationary assistant commissioner and assigned to circuit inspection of Leizhou in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 復呂塘廢渠，清鹽法。

translations.literal: He restored the abandoned Lutang canal and reformed the salt laws.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the abandoned Lutang canal and reformed the salt laws.

sentences.zh: 會罷分巡官，召還為戶部主事。

translations.literal: When circuit inspectors were abolished, he was recalled and made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When circuit inspectors were abolished, he was recalled and made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以父喪服闋，不時起，謫居安慶。

translations.literal: After completing mourning for his father, he did not resume office promptly and was demoted to reside in Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his father, he did not resume office promptly and was demoted to reside in Anqing.

sentences.zh: 建文初，復以薦知瓊州，崖州黎相仇殺，以反聞，且用兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign he was again recommended and appointed prefect of Qiongzhou; when Li tribesmen in Yazhou feuded and killed one another, it was reported as rebellion and troops were about to be deployed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign he was again recommended and appointed prefect of Qiongzhou; when Li tribesmen in Yazhou feuded and killed one another, it was reported as rebellion and troops were about to be deployed.

sentences.zh: 伯貞捕其首惡，兵遂罷。

translations.literal: Bozhen arrested the ringleaders, and the military action was called off.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen arrested the ringleaders, and the military action was called off.

sentences.zh: 瓊田歲常三獲，以賦軍，軍不時受，俟民乏，乃急斂以要利。

translations.literal: Qiong fields commonly yielded three harvests a year, levied to supply the army; the army did not accept payment on schedule but waited until the people were destitute, then collected urgently to extort profit.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong fields commonly yielded three harvests a year, levied to supply the army; the army did not accept payment on schedule but waited until the people were destitute, then collected urgently to extort profit.

sentences.zh: 伯貞為立期，三輸之，弊始絕。

translations.literal: Bozhen established fixed deadlines and three scheduled payments, and the abuse was finally ended.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen established fixed deadlines and three scheduled payments, and the abuse was finally ended.

sentences.zh: 居數年，大治，流民占籍者萬余。

translations.literal: After several years the region was greatly well governed, and more than ten thousand vagrant households were registered.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the region was greatly well governed, and more than ten thousand vagrant households were registered.

sentences.zh: 憂歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: He returned home for mourning and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home for mourning and died there.

sentences.zh: 直幼而端重，家貧力學。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi was dignified from childhood; though his family was poor, he studied diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was dignified from childhood; though his family was poor, he studied diligently.

sentences.zh: 舉永樂二年進士，改庶吉士，與曾棨、王英等二十八人同讀書文淵閣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongle, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and studied with Zeng Qi, Wang Ying, and twenty-six others in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongle, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and studied with Zeng Qi, Wang Ying, and twenty-six others in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝善其文，召入內閣，俾屬草。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his writing, summoned him into the Grand Secretariat, and had him draft documents.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his writing, summoned him into the Grand Secretariat, and had him draft documents.

sentences.zh: 尋授修撰。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷事仁宗、宣宗，累遷少詹事兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Serving through the reigns of Emperor Renzong and Emperor Xuanzong, he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Serving through the reigns of Emperor Renzong and Emperor Xuanzong, he rose to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 正統三年，《宣宗實錄》成。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong, the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengtong, the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong were completed.

sentences.zh: 進禮部侍郎，學士如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, retaining his academician post.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites while retaining his academician post.

sentences.zh: 五年出蒞部事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out to take charge of ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he went out to take charge of ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 尚書胡濙悉以部政付之，直處之若素習者。

translations.literal: Minister Hu Ying entrusted all ministry affairs to him, and Wang Zhi handled them as if long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Hu Ying entrusted all ministry affairs to him, and Wang Zhi handled them as if he had long been versed in them.

sentences.zh: 八年正月代郭琎為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he replaced Guo Jin as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year he replaced Guo Jin as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年，戶部侍郎奈亨附王振，構郎中趙敏，詞連直及侍郎曹義、趙新，並下獄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Vice Minister of Revenue Nai Heng, allied with Wang Zhen, framed bureau director Zhao Min, implicating Wang Zhi and Vice Ministers Cao Yi and Zhao Xin, and all were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Vice Minister of Revenue Nai Heng, allied with Wang Zhen, framed bureau director Zhao Min, implicating Wang Zhi and Vice Ministers Cao Yi and Zhao Xin, and all were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 三法司廷鞫，論亨斬，直等贖徒。

translations.literal: The three judicial offices tried the case in court, sentencing Heng to decapitation and Wang Zhi and the others to penal servitude redeemable by payment.
translations.idiomatic: The three judicial offices tried the case in court, sentencing Heng to decapitation and Wang Zhi and the others to penal servitude redeemable by payment.

sentences.zh: 帝宥直、義，奪亨、新俸。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned Wang Zhi and Cao Yi and confiscated the salaries of Heng and Zhao Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned Wang Zhi and Cao Yi and confiscated the salaries of Heng and Zhao Xin.

sentences.zh: 帝將親征也先，直率廷臣力諫曰：「國家備邊最為謹嚴。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to lead a personal campaign against Esen, Wang Zhi led court officials in forceful remonstrance, saying: "The state's frontier defense is maintained with the greatest rigor."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to lead a personal campaign against Esen, Wang Zhi led court officials in forceful remonstrance, saying, "The state's frontier defense is maintained with the greatest rigor."

sentences.zh: 謀臣猛將，堅甲利兵，隨處充滿，且耕且守，是以久安。

translations.literal: Strategists and fierce generals, strong armor and sharp weapons, fill every place; farming and guarding proceed together, and thus there is long peace.
translations.idiomatic: Strategists and fierce generals, strong armor and sharp weapons, fill every post; farming and guarding proceed together, and thus the realm has long enjoyed peace.

sentences.zh: 今敵肆猖獗，違天悖理，陛下但宜固封疆，申號令，堅壁清野，蓄銳以待之，可圖必勝。

translations.literal: Now the enemy runs rampant, defying heaven and violating reason; Your Majesty need only secure the borders, enforce commands, strengthen defenses and clear the countryside, and store strength to await them—then certain victory may be planned.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy runs rampant, defying heaven and violating reason; Your Majesty need only secure the borders, enforce commands, strengthen defenses and clear the countryside, and store strength to await them—then certain victory may be planned.

sentences.zh: 不必親禦六師，遠臨塞下。

translations.literal: There is no need personally to command the six armies and go far to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need for Your Majesty personally to command the six armies and go far to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 況秋署未退，旱氣未回，青草不豐，水泉猶塞，士馬之用未充。

translations.literal: Moreover, autumn heat has not yet passed, drought air has not yet turned, green grass is not abundant, water sources are still blocked, and men and horses are not fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, autumn heat has not yet passed, drought air has not yet turned, green grass is not abundant, water sources are still blocked, and men and horses are not fully supplied.

sentences.zh: 兵兇戰危，臣等以為不可。

translations.literal: War is ominous and battle perilous; we your ministers deem it inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: War is ominous and battle perilous; we your ministers deem it inadvisable.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，命直留守。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree and ordered Wang Zhi to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree and ordered Wang Zhi to remain and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 王師覆於土木。

translations.literal: The imperial army was destroyed at Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army was destroyed at Tumu.

sentences.zh: 大臣群請太后立皇子為皇太子，命郕王攝政。

translations.literal: Ministers collectively requested the empress dowager to establish the prince as crown prince and appoint the Prince of Fu as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers collectively asked the empress dowager to establish the prince as crown prince and appoint the Prince of Fu as regent.

sentences.zh: 已，勸王即位，以安反側。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they urged the prince to ascend the throne to settle unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they urged the prince to ascend the throne to settle unrest.

sentences.zh: 時變起倉卒，朝臣議屢上，皆直為首。

translations.literal: The crisis arose in sudden haste; memorials from court officials were submitted repeatedly, with Wang Zhi always leading.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis arose in sudden haste; memorials from court officials were submitted repeatedly, with Wang Zhi always leading.

sentences.zh: 而直自以不如于謙，每事推下之，雍容鎮率而已。

translations.literal: Yet Wang Zhi considered himself inferior to Yu Qian and deferred to him in every matter, remaining composed and steady in leadership.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Zhi considered himself inferior to Yu Qian and deferred to him in every matter, remaining composed and steady in leadership.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，也先使使議和，且請還上皇，下禮部議未決。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, Esen sent envoys to discuss peace and also requested the return of the retired emperor; the matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation but remained unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai, Esen sent envoys to discuss peace and also requested the return of the retired emperor; the matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation but remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 直率群臣上言曰：「太上皇惑細人言，輕身一出，至於蒙塵。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi led the officials in memorializing: "The retired emperor, misled by petty men's words, ventured forth lightly and came to suffer captivity."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi led the officials in memorializing, "The retired emperor, misled by petty men's words, ventured forth lightly and came to suffer captivity."

sentences.zh: 陛下宵衣旰食，征天下兵，與群臣兆姓同心僇力，期滅此朝食，以雪不共戴天之恥。

translations.literal: Your Majesty rises early and eats late, mobilizes armies from throughout the realm, and joins officials and the myriad people in united effort, expecting to destroy the enemy before breakfast and avenge the shame of mortal enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rises early and eats late, mobilizes armies from throughout the realm, and joins officials and the myriad people in united effort, expecting to destroy the enemy before breakfast and avenge the shame of mortal enmity.

sentences.zh: 乃者天誘其衷，也先有悔心之萌，而來求成於我，請還乘輿，此轉禍為福之機也。

translations.literal: Now heaven has moved their hearts; Esen has begun to repent and comes seeking peace with us, requesting the return of the imperial carriage—this is an opportunity to turn disaster into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Now heaven has moved their hearts; Esen has begun to repent and comes seeking peace with us, requesting the return of the imperial carriage—this is an opportunity to turn disaster into blessing.

sentences.zh: 望陛下俯從其請，遣使往報，因察其誠偽而撫納之，奉太上皇以歸，少慰祖宗之心。

translations.literal: We hope Your Majesty will graciously accede to their request, dispatch envoys in reply, observe their sincerity or deceit and receive them accordingly, and bring the retired emperor home, giving some comfort to the hearts of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: We hope Your Majesty will graciously accede to their request, dispatch envoys in reply, observe their sincerity or deceit and receive them accordingly, and bring the retired emperor home, giving some comfort to the hearts of the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 陛下天位已定，太上皇還，不復蒞天下事。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heavenly throne is already established; when the retired emperor returns, he will no longer govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's throne is already established; when the retired emperor returns, he will no longer govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下第崇奉之，則天倫厚而天眷益隆，誠古今盛事也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty simply honor and support him, then family bonds will deepen and heaven's favor will grow ever greater—truly a grand event of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty simply honor and support him, then family bonds will deepen and heaven's favor will grow ever greater—truly a grand event of past and present.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿等言良然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are indeed sound."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your words are indeed sound."

sentences.zh: 但前後使者五輩往，終不得要領。

translations.literal: But five successive missions have gone and still failed to obtain a clear answer.
translations.idiomatic: But five successive missions have gone and still failed to obtain a clear answer.

sentences.zh: 今復遣使，設彼假送駕為名，來犯京師，豈不為蒼生患。

translations.literal: If we send envoys again and they use the pretense of escorting the imperial carriage to invade the capital, would that not bring calamity upon the people?
translations.idiomatic: If we send envoys again and they use the pretense of escorting the imperial carriage to invade the capital, would that not bring calamity upon the people?

sentences.zh: 賊詐難信，其更議之。

translations.literal: The enemy's deceit is hard to trust; let the matter be reconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's deceit is hard to trust; let the matter be reconsidered.

sentences.zh: 」已而瓦剌別部阿剌使復至，胡濙等復以為言。

translations.literal: Soon afterward envoys from Ala of another Oirat branch arrived, and Hu Ying and others again spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward envoys from Ala of another Oirat branch arrived, and Hu Ying and others again spoke on the matter.

sentences.zh: 於是帝御文華殿門，召諸大臣及言官諭以宜絕狀。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor took his seat at the gate of the Wenhua Hall, summoned the chief ministers and censorial officials, and instructed them that relations ought to be severed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor took his seat at the gate of the Wenhua Hall, summoned the chief ministers and censorial officials, and instructed them that relations ought to be severed.

sentences.zh: 直對曰：「必遣使，毋貽後悔。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi replied: "Envoys must be sent—do not leave cause for regret."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi replied, "Envoys must be sent—do not leave cause for regret."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 于謙前為解，帝意釋。

translations.literal: Yu Qian stepped forward to explain, and the emperor's mood eased.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian stepped forward to explain, and the emperor's mood eased.

sentences.zh: 群臣既退，太監興安匍匐出呼曰：「若等固欲遣使，有文天祥、富弼其人乎？

translations.literal: After the officials had withdrawn, the eunuch Xing'an crawled out calling: "You insist on sending envoys—are there men like Wen Tianxiang or Fu Bi among you?"
translations.idiomatic: After the officials had withdrawn, the eunuch Xing'an crawled out calling, "You insist on sending envoys—are there men like Wen Tianxiang or Fu Bi among you?"

sentences.zh: 」直大言曰：「廷臣惟天子使，既食其祿，敢辭難乎！

translations.literal: Wang Zhi spoke loudly: "Court officials are the emperor's envoys; having received his salary, how dare we shrink from difficulty!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi spoke loudly, "Court officials are the emperor's envoys; having received his salary, how dare we shrink from difficulty!"

sentences.zh: 」言之再，聲色愈厲。

translations.literal: He spoke twice, his voice and expression growing ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke twice, his voice and expression growing ever fiercer.

sentences.zh: 安語塞，乃議遣使，命李實、羅綺往。

translations.literal: Xing'an was left speechless, and envoys were then discussed; Li Shi and Luo Qi were ordered to go.
translations.idiomatic: Xing'an was left speechless, and envoys were then discussed; Li Shi and Luo Qi were ordered to go.

sentences.zh: 既行，而瓦剌可汗脫脫不花及也先使先後至，將遣歸。

translations.literal: After they had departed, envoys from the Oirat khan Togto Buqa and from Esen arrived in succession, intending to escort the retired emperor home.
translations.idiomatic: After they had departed, envoys from the Oirat khan Togto Buqa and from Esen arrived in succession, intending to escort the retired emperor home.

sentences.zh: 使者謂館伴曰：「中國關外十四城皆為我有。

translations.literal: The envoys told the escort officials: "The fourteen cities outside the passes of China are all in our possession."
translations.idiomatic: The envoys told the escort officials, "The fourteen cities outside the passes of China are all in our possession."

sentences.zh: 前阿剌知院使來，尚遣人偕往。

translations.literal: When Commissioner Ala came before, you still sent men to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Commissioner Ala came before, you still sent men to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 今亦必得大臣同行，庶有濟。

translations.literal: Now you must also have a chief minister go together, or there will be no success.
translations.idiomatic: Now you must also have a chief minister go together, or there will be no success.

sentences.zh: 」胡濙以聞，下廷議。

translations.literal: Hu Ying reported this, and the matter was referred to court for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying reported this, and the matter was referred to court for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 直等固請，乃遣楊善等報之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi and others pressed firmly, and Yang Shan and others were dispatched in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi and others pressed firmly, and Yang Shan and others were dispatched in reply.

sentences.zh: 比實還，又以也先使至，具言也先欲和狀。

translations.literal: By the time Li Shi returned, Esen's envoys had again arrived, fully stating Esen's desire for peace.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Li Shi returned, Esen's envoys had again arrived, fully stating Esen's desire for peace.

sentences.zh: 直與寧陽侯陳懋等上疏，請更遣使賫禮幣往迎上皇，不許。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi and Marquis of Ningyang Chen Mao and others memorialized, requesting that envoys be sent again bearing gifts to welcome the retired emperor, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi and Marquis of Ningyang Chen Mao and others memorialized, requesting that envoys be sent again bearing gifts to welcome the retired emperor, but this was denied.

sentences.zh: 復上疏曰：「臣等與李實語，具得彼中情事。

translations.literal: They memorialized again: "In speaking with Li Shi, we fully learned the situation on their side."
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized again, "In speaking with Li Shi, we fully learned the situation on their side."

sentences.zh: 其所需衣物資斧者，上皇言也；

translations.literal: The clothing, supplies, and funds they need were requested by the retired emperor;
translations.idiomatic: The clothing, supplies, and funds they need were requested by the retired emperor;

sentences.zh: 而奉迎車駕，也先意也。

translations.literal: and escorting the imperial carriage was Esen's wish.
translations.idiomatic: and escorting the imperial carriage was Esen's wish.

sentences.zh: 昨者脫脫不花及阿剌知院使來，皆有報使。

translations.literal: When Togto Buqa and Commissioner Ala came before, return envoys were sent in each case.
translations.idiomatic: When Togto Buqa and Commissioner Ala came before, return envoys were sent in each case.

sentences.zh: 今也先使以迎請為辭，乃不遣使與偕，是疑敵而召兵也。

translations.literal: Now Esen's envoys use welcoming as their plea, yet no envoys are sent to accompany them—this is to distrust the enemy and invite war.
translations.idiomatic: Now Esen's envoys use welcoming as their plea, yet no envoys are sent to accompany them—this is to distrust the enemy and invite war.

sentences.zh: 」又不許。

translations.literal: Again this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Again this was denied.

sentences.zh: 已而實自言於帝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Li Shi spoke to the emperor himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Li Shi spoke to the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 帝第報也先書，就令楊善迎歸而已。

translations.literal: The emperor merely replied to Esen in writing and ordered Yang Shan to welcome the retired emperor home—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor merely replied to Esen in writing and ordered Yang Shan to welcome the retired emperor home—that was all.

sentences.zh: 直等復上言：「今北使已發，願本上皇之心，順臣民之願，因彼悔心，遣使往報，以圖迎復，此不待計而決者也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi and others memorialized again: "The northern envoys have already set out; we wish to follow the retired emperor's heart, accord with officials and people's wishes, take advantage of their repentance, and send envoys in reply to plan his welcome and return—this needs no deliberation to decide."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi and others memorialized again, "The northern envoys have already set out; we wish to follow the retired emperor's heart, accord with officials and people's wishes, take advantage of their repentance, and send envoys in reply to plan his welcome and return—this needs no deliberation to decide."

sentences.zh: 不然，眾誌難犯，違天不祥，彼將執為兵端，邊事益棘，京師亦不得高枕臥矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise the people's will cannot be violated, defying heaven is inauspicious, they will seize this as a pretext for war, frontier affairs will grow ever more urgent, and the capital too will not be able to rest in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the people's will cannot be violated, defying heaven is inauspicious, they will seize this as a pretext for war, frontier affairs will grow ever more urgent, and the capital too will not be able to rest in peace.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃命群臣擇使，直與陳懋等請仍遣實。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered officials to choose envoys; Wang Zhi and Chen Mao and others requested that Li Shi be sent again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered officials to choose envoys; Wang Zhi and Chen Mao and others asked that Li Shi be sent again.

sentences.zh: 報曰：「候善歸議之。

translations.literal: The reply was: "Wait until Shan returns, then discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: The reply was, "Wait until Shan returns, then discuss it."

sentences.zh: 」御史畢鑾等復上疏，力言：「就令彼以詐來，我以誠往，萬一不測，則我之兵力固在。

translations.literal: Censor Bi Luan and others memorialized again, forcefully stating: "Even if they come with deceit and we go with sincerity, if anything unforeseen occurs, our military strength remains intact."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Bi Luan and others memorialized again, forcefully stating, "Even if they come with deceit and we go with sincerity, if anything unforeseen occurs, our military strength remains intact."

sentences.zh: 」帝終不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately would not listen.

sentences.zh: 已而善竟奉上皇還。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Shan did indeed escort the retired emperor home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Shan did indeed escort the retired emperor home.

sentences.zh: 二年，也先遣使入貢，且請答使。

translations.literal: In the second year, Esen sent envoys to offer tribute and also requested return envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Esen sent envoys to offer tribute and also requested return envoys.

sentences.zh: 直屢疏言：「邊備未修，芻糧未積，瘡痍未復，宜如其請。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi repeatedly memorialized: "Frontier defenses are not yet repaired, fodder and grain are not yet stored, wounds are not yet healed—His Majesty ought to accede to their request."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi memorialized repeatedly that frontier defenses were not yet repaired, fodder and grain not yet stockpiled, and the realm not yet healed from its wounds, and that the emperor ought to grant their request.

sentences.zh: 遣使往以觀虛實，開導其善。

translations.literal: Send envoys to observe their true condition and guide them toward what is good.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys should be sent to gauge their true intentions and guide them toward reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 無何，也先遣騎入塞，以報使為辭。

translations.literal: Before long, Esen sent horsemen across the frontier, using the lack of return envoys as his pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Esen sent horsemen across the frontier, citing the failure to send return envoys as his excuse.

sentences.zh: 直與群臣復請之，卒不許。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi and the officials again requested it, but in the end it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi and the officials pressed again, but the emperor still refused.

sentences.zh: 直等乃上疏言：「陛下銳意治兵，為戰守計，真大有為之主。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi and others then memorialized: "Your Majesty is keen to train troops and plan for offense and defense—a ruler truly capable of great undertakings."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi and others then memorialized that the emperor's resolve to train troops and plan for both offense and defense showed him to be a ruler truly capable of great undertakings.

sentences.zh: 然使命不通，難保其不為寇。

translations.literal: Yet if missions do not pass, it is hard to guarantee they will not become raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet without diplomatic contact, there was no guarantee they would not raid again.

sentences.zh: 宜敕沿邊守臣，發兵遊僥，有警則入保，無事則力耕。

translations.literal: Frontier garrison officials ought to be ordered to send troops on patrol; when there is alarm they should enter fortified posts, and when there is peace they should labor at farming.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanders ought to be ordered to patrol with troops, withdraw into fortified posts when alarmed, and farm diligently when at peace.

sentences.zh: 陛下於機務之暇，時召京營總督、總兵，詢以方略，誠接而禮貌之，信賞罰以持其後，斯戰守可言也。

translations.literal: In intervals from state affairs, Your Majesty should summon the capital garrison commanders and regional generals, inquire into strategy, receive them sincerely and treat them with courtesy, and rely on rewards and punishments to sustain them thereafter—then offense and defense may be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: In intervals from state affairs, Your Majesty should summon the capital garrison commanders and regional generals, consult them on strategy, receive them with sincerity and courtesy, and sustain them through fair rewards and punishments—only then could offense and defense be truly secured.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰「善」。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 明年正月進少傅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he was promoted to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he was promoted to Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 帝欲易太子。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to replace the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to replace the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 未發。

translations.literal: The matter had not yet been initiated.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet acted on the plan.

sentences.zh: 會思明土知府黃矰以為請。

translations.literal: It happened that Huang Wei, native prefect of Siming, requested it on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Then Huang Wei, native prefect of Siming, memorialized requesting the change.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，下禮部議。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and referred the matter to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and referred the matter to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 胡濙唯唯，文武諸臣議者九十一人當署名，直有難色。

translations.literal: Hu Ying assented vaguely; the ninety-one civil and military officials who deliberated were to sign, and Wang Zhi showed reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying assented without conviction; ninety-one civil and military officials were to sign the deliberation, and Wang Zhi looked deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 陳循濡筆強之，乃署，竟易皇太子。

translations.literal: Chen Xun dipped the brush and forced him; he then signed, and the crown prince was finally changed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun dipped the brush and pressed him until he signed, and the heir apparent was replaced.

sentences.zh: 直進兼太子太師，賜金幣加等。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi was promoted to concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and granted gold and currency of higher grade.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was promoted to concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and granted gold and currency of the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 頓足嘆曰：「此何等大事，乃為一蠻酋所壞，吾輩愧死矣。

translations.literal: He stamped his foot and sighed: "What a momentous affair, ruined by a single barbarian chieftain—we ought to die of shame."
translations.idiomatic: He stamped his foot and sighed, "What a momentous affair, undone by a single tribal chieftain—we ought to die of shame."

sentences.zh: 」景帝疾亟，直、濙等會諸大臣臺諫，請復立沂王為皇太子，推大學士商輅草疏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingtai's illness grew critical, Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, and others convened chief ministers and censorial officials, requesting that the Prince of Yi be re-established as crown prince, and entrusted Grand Secretary Shang Lu to draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingtai's illness grew critical, Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, and others convened chief ministers and censorial officials to request that the Prince of Yi be re-established as heir apparent, and asked Grand Secretary Shang Lu to draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 未上，而石亨、徐有貞等奪門迎上皇復位，殺王文等。

translations.literal: Before it was submitted, Shi Heng, Xu Youzhen, and others seized the gate to welcome the retired emperor's restoration and killed Wang Wen and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before it could be submitted, Shi Heng, Xu Youzhen, and others forced open the gate to restore the retired emperor and killed Wang Wen and the others.

sentences.zh: 疏草留姚夔所，嘗出以示郎中陸昶，嘆曰：「是疏不及進，天也。

translations.literal: The draft remained with Yao Kui; he once showed it to bureau director Lu Chang and sighed: "That this memorial was not submitted in time was heaven's will."
translations.idiomatic: The draft remained with Yao Kui, who once showed it to bureau director Lu Chang and sighed, "That this memorial never reached the throne was heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 」直遂乞休。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi then requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi then asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 賜璽書、金綺、楮幣，給驛歸。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial letter, gold brocade, and paper currency, and given an imperial courier for his return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an imperial letter, gold brocade, and paper currency, and sent home with an imperial courier.

sentences.zh: 直為人方面修髯，儀觀甚偉。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi had a square face and long beard; his bearing was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi had a square face and flowing beard, and an imposing presence.

sentences.zh: 性嚴重，不茍言笑。

translations.literal: His nature was grave; he was not casual in speech or laughter.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave by nature and never casual in speech or laughter.

sentences.zh: 及與人交，恂恂如也。

translations.literal: Yet in dealing with others he was respectful and deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in dealing with others he was respectful and unassuming.

sentences.zh: 在翰林二十余年，稽古代言編纂紀註之事，多出其手。

translations.literal: Having served in the Hanlin Academy for more than twenty years, he handled most matters of classical research, imperial drafting, compilation, and annotation.
translations.idiomatic: During more than twenty years in the Hanlin Academy, he handled most of the court's classical research, imperial drafting, compilation, and annotation.

sentences.zh: 與金溪王英齊名，人稱「二王」，以居地目直曰「東王」，英曰「西王」。

translations.literal: He was famed alongside Wang Ying of Jinxi; people called them the Two Wangs, naming Wang Zhi the Eastern King and Wang Ying the Western King by their residences.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed alongside Wang Ying of Jinxi; people called them the Two Wangs, naming Wang Zhi the Eastern King and Wang Ying the Western King according to where they lived.

sentences.zh: 直以次當入閣，楊士奇不欲也。

translations.literal: By seniority Wang Zhi ought to have entered the Grand Secretariat, but Yang Shiqi did not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: By seniority Wang Zhi ought to have entered the Grand Secretariat, but Yang Shiqi opposed it.

sentences.zh: 及長吏部，兼廉慎。

translations.literal: When he headed the Ministry of Personnel, he was additionally incorruptible and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: When he headed the Ministry of Personnel, he became still more incorruptible and cautious.

sentences.zh: 時初罷廷臣薦舉方面大吏，專屬吏部。

translations.literal: At that time court recommendation of regional governors had just been abolished, and the power belonged solely to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the practice of court recommendation for regional governors had just been abolished, leaving appointments solely to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 直委任曹郎，嚴抑奔競。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi entrusted bureau directors and strictly suppressed scrambling for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi entrusted his bureau directors and strictly suppressed scrambling for advancement.

sentences.zh: 凡御史巡方歸者，必令具所屬賢否以備選擢，稱得人。

translations.literal: Whenever censors returned from regional inspection, he required them to report the merit or demerit of officials under their jurisdiction for selection and promotion; he was said to obtain the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever censors returned from regional inspection, he required reports on the merit of officials under their jurisdiction for promotion, and was praised for appointing the right men.

sentences.zh: 其子資為南國子博士。

translations.literal: His son Ji was a doctorate fellow at the Southern Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Ji served as a doctorate fellow at the Southern Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 考績至部，文選郎欲留侍直，直不可，曰：「是亂法自我始也。

translations.literal: When his performance review came to the ministry, the personnel selection director wished to retain him to attend Wang Zhi, but Wang Zhi would not agree, saying: "To disorder the law would begin with me."
translations.idiomatic: When his performance review came to the ministry, the personnel selection director wished to keep him at Wang Zhi's side, but Wang Zhi refused, saying, "To bend the law would begin with me."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷以直老，命何文淵為尚書佐之。

translations.literal: Because Wang Zhi was old, the court appointed He Wenyuan as minister to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wang Zhi was growing old, the court appointed He Wenyuan as minister to assist him.

sentences.zh: 文淵去，又命王翺，部遂有二尚書。

translations.literal: When Wenyuan left, Wang Ao was appointed, and the ministry then had two ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyuan left, Wang Ao was appointed, and the ministry briefly had two ministers.

sentences.zh: 直為尚書十四年，年益高，名德日益重。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi served as minister for fourteen years; as his years grew greater, his reputation and virtue grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi served as minister for fourteen years, and as he grew older his reputation and moral weight only increased.

sentences.zh: 帝優禮之，免其常朝。

translations.literal: The emperor treated him with special courtesy and exempted him from regular court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him with special courtesy and exempted him from regular court attendance.

sentences.zh: 比家居，嘗從諸佃仆耕蒔，擊鼓歌唱。

translations.literal: When he was at home, he would join tenant laborers in plowing and planting, beating drums and singing.
translations.idiomatic: At home he would join his tenant laborers in plowing and planting, beating drums and singing as he worked.

sentences.zh: 諸子孫更叠舉觴上壽，直嘆曰：「曩者西楊抑我，令不得共事。

translations.literal: His sons and grandsons took turns raising cups to wish him long life; Wang Zhi sighed: "Formerly Western Yang kept me down and would not let me serve together with him."
translations.idiomatic: His sons and grandsons took turns raising cups to wish him long life, and Wang Zhi sighed, "Formerly Yang Shiqi kept me out of the Grand Secretariat and would not let me serve with him."

sentences.zh: 然使我在閣，今上復辟，當不免遼陽之行，安得與汝曹為樂哉！

translations.literal: Yet if I had been in the Secretariat when the present emperor was restored, I would surely not have escaped exile to Liaoyang—how could I enjoy this happiness with you!
translations.idiomatic: Yet if I had served in the Secretariat when the present emperor was restored, I would surely not have escaped exile to Liaoyang—how could I be enjoying this happiness with you now!

sentences.zh: 」天順六年卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Tianshun, at the age of eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Tianshun, at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚文端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 資仕至翰林檢討，亦以學行稱。

translations.literal: Ji rose to Hanlin reviser and was also praised for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji rose to Hanlin reviser and was likewise praised for learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 曾孫思，自有傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Si has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Wang Si has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高谷之清直，胡濙之寬厚，王直之端重，蓋皆有大臣之度焉。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Gao Gu's uprightness, Hu Ying's generosity, Wang Zhi's dignity—all possessed the measure of great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Gao Gu's uprightness, Hu Ying's generosity, and Wang Zhi's dignity—all showed the bearing of great ministers.

sentences.zh: 當英、景之間，國勢初更，人心觀望，執政任事之臣多阿意取容。

translations.literal: Between the Ying and Jing reigns, the state's situation was newly changing, people's hearts were watchful, and many ministers in power curried favor to please others.
translations.idiomatic: Between the reigns of Yingzong and Jingtai the state was in upheaval, the people watched and waited, and many ministers in power curried favor to please their superiors.

sentences.zh: 而谷、濙忄卷忄卷於迎駕之儀，直侃侃於遣使之請，皆力持正議，不隨眾俯仰，故能身負碩望，始終一節，可謂老成人矣。

translations.literal: Yet Gao Gu and Hu Ying were earnestly concerned over the welcoming ceremony, and Wang Zhi spoke forthrightly on sending envoys; all forcefully upheld correct views and did not follow the crowd in bowing and rising, and therefore could bear great renown, maintaining one integrity to the end—truly men of mature judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gao Gu and Hu Ying were earnestly concerned over the welcome ceremony, and Wang Zhi spoke forthrightly in urging the dispatch of envoys; all held firm to correct views and refused to follow the crowd, and so they bore great renown and maintained their integrity to the end—truly men of mature judgment.
